archetypes.name: threshold-denominator
archetypes.rationale: The >50% gate uses a variable denominator (4 vs 8) driven by STATIC_SLOT_COUNT; DROPPED_SLOTS_FILE adds failures additively; review-core.sh must not recompute the denominator from availability booleans — all three sources must stay consistent or the gate misfires silently.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the >50% failure-threshold computation end-to-end: verify STATIC_SLOT_COUNT is the sole denominator source and is never recomputed from availability booleans in review-core.sh or check-reviewer-failure-threshold.sh. Check that DROPPED_SLOTS_FILE rows counted as additional FAILED_SLOTS apply only to static (non-dyn-*) slots, and that the dyn-* exclusion in is_dynamic_reviewer_basename covers both Cursor and Codex dynamic basename variants. Confirm the boundary cases: 1-of-8 failures must yield THRESHOLD_OK=true and 5-of-8 must yield THRESHOLD_OK=false; verify the plan's 4-slot default (--intended-slots 4) and 8-slot both-vendor path both satisfy the >50% math. Check that partial static dispatch (STATIC_DISPATCH_OK=false with one dropped peer and the opposite vendor peer succeeding) does NOT hard-stop the panel without running threshold math. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: vendor-gate-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan threads three new inter-script KV signals (DROPPED_SLOTS_FILE, codex_present_for_waterfall, conditional --no-fallback) through dispatch-panel.sh → review-core.sh → check-reviewer-failure-threshold.sh; any missing forwarding step or wrong gate condition silently breaks the both-vendor path or the dropped-peer accounting.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify the inter-script KV handoff chain: confirm DROPPED_SLOTS_FILE is emitted on dispatch-panel.sh stdout, parsed in review-core.sh, and forwarded to check-reviewer-failure-threshold.sh via --dropped-slots-file — checking that no intermediate script drops it. Verify codex_present_for_waterfall="$CODEX_AVAILABLE" is set before the single dispatch-with-waterfall.sh invocation and that --codex-present is passed consistently, mirroring dispatch-plan-review-panel.sh. Check that --no-fallback is appended to the waterfall invocation only when CURSOR_AVAILABLE=true AND CODEX_AVAILABLE=true, and is absent for single-vendor and both-down cases — verify the plan's claimed conditional gate matches actual script logic in the file. Confirm that the plan's stated divergences from dispatch-plan-review-panel.sh (conditional vs always --no-fallback, partial-drop vs total-dispatch failure semantics) are internally consistent and do not create unreachable code paths. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: regression-reversal
archetypes.rationale: The plan explicitly reverses #2449 (codex_present_for_waterfall=false → =$CODEX_AVAILABLE) without stating what triggered the original disable; if the original failure mode still exists and the new guards (conditional --no-fallback, larch-log exclusion) do not cover it, the regression silently reappears.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the #2449 reversal: read any available context in dispatch-panel.sh comments, commit history references, or dispatch-with-waterfall.sh to determine why codex_present_for_waterfall was originally hardcoded to false — then assess whether the plan's new guards (conditional --no-fallback, larch-log static codex-specialist-* exclusion, CODEX_AVAILABLE gating) adequately prevent the original failure mode from recurring. Check that the larch-log.sh deny pattern for static codex-specialist-*-output.txt is precise enough not to match dyn-*-codex-output.txt basenames, and not too narrow to miss sidecar files (phase/retry suffix variants) that static Cursor exclusion already covers. Verify that the plan's failure mode 5 mitigation (CODEX_PRESENT gating, no duplicate fallback, #3463 pruner later) is sufficient as an interim guard before #3463 lands, and flag any gap where re-enabling Codex without the pruner could produce runaway spend or duplicate findings in the current implementation surface. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
